intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2EE (CMT2EE) is caused by homozygous mutation in the MPV17 gene (137960) on chromosome 2p23.3.

checks.claim: Axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2EE (CMT2EE) is caused by homozygous mutation in the MPV17 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we describe five additional patients from two unrelated families with sensorimotor axonal neuropathy without hepatocerebral affection caused by homozygous MPV17 variants
checks.explanation: The paper links homozygous MPV17 variants to axonal sensorimotor neuropathy. The CMT2EE label is OMIM nomenclature.

checks.claim: The MPV17 gene is located on chromosome 2p23.3.
checks.evidence_quote: the POLG (NM_002693), DGUOK (NM_080918) and MPV17 (NM_002437.4) genes were amplified
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is not stated in the paper but is standard nomenclature, which the instructions count as supported.

paragraphs.text: Axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2EE (CMT2EE) is an autosomal recessive axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy that begins in childhood, adolescence, or adulthood. It causes distal muscle weakness and atrophy, mainly in the lower limbs, along with distal sensory loss and areflexia (Choi et al., 2015; Baumann et al., 2019). Most reported patients had no liver or brain involvement. However, Blakely et al. (2012) described a patient whose neuropathy was accompanied by leukoencephalopathy, hepatic steatosis and fibrosis, and multiple mtDNA deletions in muscle.

checks.claim: CMT2EE is an autosomal recessive axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: This study enrolled two autosomal recessive Korean families with axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy (FC26 and FC355, Fig. 1a).

checks.claim: CMT2EE begins in childhood, adolescence, or adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: two unrelated neuropathy patients (9 and 13 years of age) with onset of the syndrome
checks.explanation: Paper supports childhood/adolescent onset only; adulthood onset is not from this paper.

checks.claim: CMT2EE causes distal muscle weakness and atrophy, mainly in the lower limbs.
checks.evidence_quote: Neurologic examination at the age of 34 years revealed muscle weakness and atrophies of bilateral, distal muscles, predominantly in the lower limbs.

checks.claim: CMT2EE causes distal sensory loss and areflexia.
checks.evidence_quote: Like patient one, he complained that vibration and position senses were more severely disturbed than pain and touch senses, and he was able to walk with assistance. Deep tendon reflexes, in all extremities, were absent.

checks.claim: Most reported patients with CMT2EE had no liver or brain involvement.
checks.evidence_quote: But, the present two patients showed only axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, and they did not exhibit any liver or brain abnormalities, at the ages of 34 and 22 years.
checks.explanation: Paper reports only its two patients lacking liver/brain involvement; 'most reported patients' generalization is not from this paper.

checks.claim: Blakely et al. (2012) described a CMT2EE patient whose neuropathy was accompanied by leukoencephalopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: We describe a patient presenting with a severe peripheral neuropathy, leukoencephalopathy and liver involvement due to a homozygous MPV17 gene mutation

checks.evidence_quote: liver biopsy confirmed patchy steatosis (∼20%) with early bridging fibrosis
checks.explanation: Hepatic steatosis and fibrosis are stated.

checks.claim: Blakely et al. (2012) described a CMT2EE patient with multiple mtDNA deletions in muscle.
checks.evidence_quote: Long-range PCR amplification showed the presence of multiple mtDNA deletions (Fig. 3a), confirming a disorder of mtDNA maintenance.
checks.explanation: Multiple mtDNA deletions in muscle are stated.

paragraphs.text: Blakely et al. (2012) reported a 21-year-old Pakistani man, born to nonconsanguineous parents, who had difficulty walking from age 14 years. Over several years this progressed to bilateral foot drop, which required orthoses, and distal numbness. On examination he had distal muscle wasting and weakness, clawed toes, areflexia, distal sensory loss, and mild hepatomegaly. He did not have pes cavus or significant cognitive impairment. Nerve conduction studies showed an axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, and sural nerve biopsy showed a severe chronic axonal neuropathy. Cranial MRI showed diffuse T2-hyperintense signal in the cerebral and cerebellar white matter, which the authors considered suggestive of leukoencephalopathy; an MRI at age 9 years had been normal. CSF protein (1963 mg/L) and CSF lactate (4.3 mmol/L) were raised. Liver biopsy showed patchy steatosis with early bridging fibrosis, although the patient had no clinically significant chronic liver disease. His sister had a progressive, fatal hepatitis at age 9 years. Their father had an episode of hepatitis in childhood and recovered fully.

paragraphs.text: Choi et al. (2015) reported 2 unrelated Korean patients, each born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents. Patient 1 (family FC26) was a 34-year-old woman with normal early motor milestones. She first noticed distal lower limb weakness at 9 years of age and walked with short leg braces from age 12. At 34 years she had distal muscle weakness and atrophy, predominantly in the lower limbs, with severe atrophy of the intrinsic hand, foot, and calf muscles. She also had flexion deformities of the interphalangeal joints, ankle joint deformity, and scoliosis. Vibration and position sense were more disturbed than pain and touch, and knee and ankle jerks were absent. She had no growth retardation, gastrointestinal dysmotility, hepatomegaly, cognitive impairment, ophthalmoplegia, corneal scarring, or hypoglycemic attacks. Serum lactate was mildly elevated (2.1 mmol/L), and liver enzymes, glucose, and pyruvate were normal.

paragraphs.text: Electrophysiologic findings were similar in the 2 patients of Choi et al. (2015). Sural sensory nerve action potentials were lost early in the disease. Median and ulnar motor conduction velocities and CMAPs were decreased, peroneal and tibial CMAPs could not be elicited, and no sensory responses were obtained. Visual and brainstem auditory evoked potentials were normal. Lower leg MRI showed severe atrophy and fatty replacement, predominantly of the soleus muscles, with relative sparing of the tibialis posterior and lateral gastrocnemius. The authors considered this pattern consistent with length-dependent axonal degeneration and similar to CMT2A. Brain MRI was normal. Sural nerve biopsy from patient 1 at age 34 showed almost complete loss of large and medium-sized myelinated fibers (10/mm2) with a few small myelinated fibers remaining. Unmyelinated axons showed atrophy and vesicular changes, and there was no demyelination, remyelination, or onion bulb formation. Vastus lateralis biopsy from patient 2 at age 22 showed increased, irregular NADH-TR and SDH reaction, a few ragged-red fibers, and subsarcolemmal accumulation of enlarged mitochondria.

paragraphs.text: Choi et al. (2015) used whole-exome sequencing in 2 unrelated Korean patients with autosomal recessive axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy without liver or brain involvement. Both carried a homozygous c.122G-A transition in the MPV17 gene, resulting in an arg41-to-gln (R41Q) substitution at a conserved residue. Sanger sequencing confirmed the mutation, and a mutant allele was putatively inherited from each parent. The variant was absent from 300 controls, from in-house exomes (n = 302), and from dbSNP142 and 1000 Genomes. It was present at very low frequency in ESP (0.00008) and ExAC (0.00002471). In NSC34 mouse motor neuronal cells, knockdown of Mpv17 significantly reduced cell proliferation and viability against reactive oxygen species and affected OXPHOS levels. Overexpression of the R41Q mutant protein significantly inhibited cell proliferation compared with controls, as did overexpression of the R50Q and L143* mutants. The authors suggested that both loss of normal MPV17 function and detrimental gain-of-function effects of the mutant protein might impair neuronal function.

Their patients had only axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy at ages 34 and 22 years. The authors also noted a milder phenotype in patients with an R41W mutation at the same residue, and that R41W overexpression likewise affected cellular proliferation. They suggested that mutation at arg41 predominantly causes peripheral neuropathy.

paragraphs.text: Blakely et al. (2012) studied a 21-year-old Pakistani man with axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, leukoencephalopathy, hepatic steatosis with early bridging fibrosis, and multiple mtDNA deletions in muscle. He was homozygous for a missense mutation in the MPV17 gene, reported as c.2898C-T (c.298C-T in the figure legend), resulting in a pro98-to-leu (P98L) substitution at a residue conserved from human to yeast. The mutation had previously been reported as recessive in a patient with mtDNA depletion in liver. Parental samples were not available. The parents were not known to be consanguineous, but the authors suggested they shared a common ancestor.
